questions.q:
For non-negative integers \(s\) and \(r\), let \(\dbinom sr=\begin{cases}\dfrac{s!}{r!(s-r)!}&\text{if }r\le s,\\0&\text{if }r>s.\end{cases}\)
For positive integers \(m\) and \(n\), let \(g(m,n)=\sum\limits_{p=0}^{m+n}\dfrac{f(m,n,p)}{\dbinom{n+p}p}\) where for any non-negative integer \(p\), \(f(m,n,p)=\sum\limits_{i=0}^p\dbinom mi\dbinom{n+i}p\dbinom{p+n}{p-i}\).
Then which of the following statements is/are TRUE?
questions.sol: \(\dfrac{\binom{n+i}p\binom{p+n}{p-i}}{\binom{n+p}p}=\dbinom n{p-i}\), so \(\dfrac{f(m,n,p)}{\binom{n+p}p}=\sum\limits_i\dbinom mi\dbinom n{p-i}=\dbinom{m+n}p\) and \(g(m,n)=2^{m+n}\). Hence (a), (b) hold, \(g(2m,2n)=2^{2m+2n}=(g(m,n))^2\), and (c) fails.

If \((1+x)^n=C_0+C_1x+C_2x^2+\ldots+C_nx^n\), then show that the sum of the products of the \(C_i\)'s is taken two at a time represented by \(\sum\limits_{0\le i<j\le n}C_iC_j\) is equal to \(2^{2n-1}-\dfrac{(2n)!}{2(n!)^2}\).

Given \(s_n=1+q+q^2+\ldots+q^n\), \(S_n=1+\left(\dfrac{q+1}2\right)+\left(\dfrac{q+1}2\right)^2+\ldots+\left(\dfrac{q+1}2\right)^n\), \(q\ne1\)
Prove that \({}^{n+1}C_1+{}^{n+1}C_2s_1+{}^{n+1}C_3s_2+\ldots+{}^{n+1}C_{n+1}s_n=2^nS_n\).
questions.sol: \(s_k=\dfrac{1-q^{k+1}}{1-q}\), so the left side is \(\dfrac1{1-q}\sum\limits_{k=0}^n{}^{n+1}C_{k+1}(1-q^{k+1})=\dfrac{(2^{n+1}-1)-((1+q)^{n+1}-1)}{1-q}=\dfrac{2^{n+1}-(1+q)^{n+1}}{1-q}\). Also \(2^nS_n=2^n\cdot\dfrac{1-\left(\frac{1+q}2\right)^{n+1}}{1-\frac{1+q}2}\), which is the same.

questions.q: Find the sum of the series \(\sum\limits_{r=0}^n(-1)^r\,{}^nC_r\left[\dfrac1{2^r}+\dfrac{3^r}{2^{2r}}+\dfrac{7^r}{2^{3r}}+\dfrac{15^r}{2^{4r}}+\ldots\text{ upto }m\text{ terms}\right]\)
questions.sol: The \(k\)th bracket term is \(\left(\dfrac{2^k-1}{2^k}\right)^r\), and \(\sum\limits_r(-1)^r\,{}^nC_rt^r=(1-t)^n\). So the sum is \(\sum\limits_{k=1}^m\left(\dfrac1{2^k}\right)^n=\dfrac{\frac1{2^n}\left(1-\frac1{2^{mn}}\right)}{1-\frac1{2^n}}\).

questions.q: Let \(R=(5\sqrt5+11)^{2n+1}\) and \(f=R-[R]\), where \([\cdot]\) denotes the greatest integer function. Prove that \(Rf=4^{2n+1}\).
questions.sol: Let \(G=(5\sqrt5-11)^{2n+1}\); \(0<G<1\). \(R-G\) is an integer (the odd powers of \(5\sqrt5\) cancel), so \(f=G\). Then \(Rf=RG=(125-121)^{2n+1}=4^{2n+1}\).

questions.q: If \(\sum\limits_{r=0}^{2n}a_r(x-2)^r=\sum\limits_{r=0}^{2n}b_r(x-3)^r\) and \(a_k=1\) for all \(k\ge n\), then show that \(b_n={}^{2n+1}C_{n+1}\)
Prove that \(\sum\limits_{r=1}^k(-3)^{r-1}\,{}^{3n}C_{2r-1}=0\) where \(k=\dfrac{3n}2\) and \(n\) is an even positive integer.
questions.sol: The imaginary part of \((1+i\sqrt3)^{3n}\) is \(\sqrt3\sum\limits_{r=1}^k(-3)^{r-1}\,{}^{3n}C_{2r-1}\). But \((1+i\sqrt3)^{3n}=2^{3n}e^{in\pi}\) is real, so the sum is \(0\).

questions.q: Let \(n\) be a \(+\)ve integer and \((1+x+x^2)^n=a_0+a_1x+\ldots+a_{2n}x^{2n}\), then show that \(a_0^2-a_1^2+\ldots+a_{2n}^2=a_n\)
questions.sol: Replacing \(x\) by \(-\frac1x\) and multiplying by \(x^{2n}\): \((x^2-x+1)^n=\sum(-1)^ra_rx^{2n-r}\). Multiply by the given expansion: \((1+x^2+x^4)^n=\sum a_rx^r\cdot\sum(-1)^ra_rx^{2n-r}\). The coefficient of \(x^{2n}\) is \(a_n\) on the left and \(\sum(-1)^ra_r^2\) on the right.
